title: Devin Operating Card
summary: Delegate bounded repository work to Devin with explicit success criteria, reviewed Knowledge and Playbooks, and pull-request evidence.
prerequisites: A repository connection limited to required projects

sections.title: Delegate outcomes that can be independently reviewed
paragraphs: Cognition describes Devin as an AI software engineering agent for longer-lived software tasks against connected repositories. Its first-run guidance includes asking for task scopes, repository inquiry and planning, and selecting a repository and agent. The documentation also describes reusable Knowledge and Playbooks. Choose Devin for bounded work whose environment, required inputs, expected result, and tests can be stated before the session starts. Source: Cognition, Your first Devin session, https://docs.devin.ai/get-started/first-run.

Grant access only to the repositories and external systems the task needs. Treat attached Knowledge and Playbooks as recorded operational inputs. Cognition describes Playbooks as reusable guides that specify an outcome, procedure, specifications, advice, forbidden actions, and required user input. Attach and inspect the applicable Playbook before starting. Source: Cognition, Creating Devin Playbooks, https://docs.devin.ai/product-guides/creating-playbooks.

Good candidates have a reviewable artifact, a bounded scope, deterministic checks, and a clear stop condition. Poor candidates include open-ended architecture changes, tasks requiring unverified production authority, or work where success depends on an unrecorded human judgment. Devin can modify code, run commands, and create pull requests according to the first-run documentation. These capabilities do not by themselves establish permission enforcement, branch protection, review approval, or merge authority.

code.label: Product operation facts
code.code:
Before starting a Devin task:
1. State the desired repository outcome and acceptance tests.
2. Ask Devin to inspect the repository and plan the work.
3. Choose the approved repository and agent.
4. Attach the applicable Knowledge and Playbook.
5. Inspect the proposed plan and confirm scope.
6. Allow only the repository work needed for the task.
7. Review the diff, test evidence, and pull request before acceptance.

The first-run documentation describes code modification, command execution, and pull-request creation. It does not establish that Devin enforces every operator-written boundary.

sections.title: Define delivery and forbidden actions
paragraphs: Start with clear success criteria, the target branch, environment setup, required artifacts, and forbidden actions. Prefer a reviewable branch or pull request over direct default-branch mutation. These are operating practices for controlled delegation, not claims that Devin enforces a particular workflow.

Monitor the session for blocked assumptions and scope changes. Review the complete diff, test evidence, and external side effects before merging or accepting the result. Specific workspace permissions, branch protections, session-monitoring controls, and recovery controls require verification in the applicable Cognition documentation and workspace administrator policy.

The following filled Playbook is a fictional planning example for this learning resource. It specifies what an operator should request and inspect. It is not evidence that a Devin session, branch, pull request, permission change, or external action occurred. Recording a Playbook or Knowledge revision is recommended operational practice here, not a claim that Devin provides built-in versioning.

code.label: Filled Playbook for a shipping task
code.code:
Name: Small predicate change with focused tests
Revision: 2 (operator-maintained record for this exercise)

Outcome:
Change the order-shipping eligibility predicate in the connected acme-orders repository so an order is shippable only when status is exactly "ready" and hold is exactly false. Add or update focused tests for the accepted case, a held ready order, and a changed non-ready order. Deliver the change for review without changing unrelated files.

Procedure:
1. Inspect the repository and the existing test instructions.
2. Confirm the approved revision and task branch.
3. Locate the shipping predicate and its focused tests.
4. Make the smallest implementation change.
5. Run the focused test command.
6. Inspect the complete diff and report any scope change.
7. Create a pull request if that action is authorized. Do not merge.

Specifications:
Repository: acme-orders
Branch: task/shipping-eligibility
Allowed files: src/shipping.js and test/shipping.test.js, plus one directly related test configuration file only if required by the existing test runner
Required cases: ready and not held is true; ready and held is false; packed and not held is false

Advice:
Use the repository's existing conventions. Preserve existing tests. Explain the predicate change and include test output in the handoff.

Forbidden actions:
Do not edit unrelated files. Do not weaken, delete, or rewrite tests to make them pass. Do not change dependency versions. Do not commit secrets. Do not use production data or credentials. Do not make network calls. Do not install packages. Do not merge. Do not push to the default branch. Do not run broad destructive commands. Do not delete the working directory.

Required user input:
Issue: ACME-1842
Approved repository and revision: [operator supplies these]
Knowledge: Order status meanings, revision 3 [operator confirms attachment]
Authorized permissions and branch policy: [operator supplies these]

Verification:
Confirm the branch diff contains only intended implementation and tests. Run the existing focused test command. Confirm all three required cases. Obtain independent review of the proposed diff. Check the stated repository postcondition only after an approved merge.

Recovery:
If scope or assumptions diverge, stop or close the session if that control is available, preserve the prompt and activity evidence, inspect the isolated branch, revert only task-branch changes when authorized, reconcile external side effects, and restart with a smaller task. Do not assume that closing a session reverses external actions.

sections.title: Reusable delegation task card
paragraphs: Use this template to make a delegation request reviewable. Replace each bracketed field before sending it to an agent. The template is not a record of a real product configuration.

code.label: Reusable delegation card
code.code:
Task: [one reviewable repository outcome]
Scope: [repository, branch, services, and data]
Permissions: [repo, network, secrets, and external systems]
Inputs: [issue, Knowledge, Playbook, and environment]
Forbidden actions: [explicit boundaries]
Verification: [tests, PR review, and postconditions]
Recovery: [close session, revert branch, reconcile side effects]

sections.title: Expected evidence and verification
paragraphs: Expected evidence for a real delegated change should include the submitted task prompt, the identifiers or operator-maintained revisions of attached Knowledge and Playbook material when available, session activity, the branch diff, test output, independent pull-request review, and checks for relevant external postconditions. This card presents that list as an audit checklist. It does not claim that any listed evidence exists for this resource.

If the session diverges, stop or steer it, preserve the evidence, close unneeded access where authorized, inspect and revert the isolated branch or affected resources, and restart from a smaller task. Reconcile side effects separately because branch reversal does not necessarily undo actions outside the repository.

Distinguish three kinds of evidence: a local simulation proves only what the local files and commands show; a product-session record proves what the recorded session did; and an external postcondition check proves what happened in the connected system. The exercise below supplies only local simulation evidence. It supplies no Devin session evidence, branch or pull-request evidence, authority evidence, review evidence, or recovery evidence.

sections.title: Local simulation: repair one wrong predicate
paragraphs: Use Bash for setup; on Windows, Git Bash is recommended. Check `node --version`; this exercise intends Node 22. Save `shipping.js`, `shipping.test.js`, and the optional `shipping.answer.js` inside the created `devin-operating-card-exercise` directory, alongside its auto-created `package.json`. Change into that directory before running commands. Keep the answer file separate and optional, and do not overwrite the learner starter files.

This dependency-free exercise simulates the implementation and verification portions of the fictional task card. It does not connect to Devin, a repository host, a pull-request system, production, or any external service. It is intended for Node.js 22 and uses only built-in Node.js functionality.

The setup creates a fresh directory and a local package.json with type set to commonjs. This makes the CommonJS .js files work even when the parent directory or repository uses type:module. Do not use the setup in a directory containing work you need to preserve. The setup refuses to continue if its exercise directory already exists.

The starter implementation contains one deliberately wrong predicate. The immutable test file checks three cases: an accepted ready order, a held ready order that must be rejected, and a changed-input case in which status changes from ready to packed and must be rejected. The test reports every case before exiting, so the broken baseline exposes both predicate failures instead of aborting at the first assertion. Do not edit the test file.

code.label: Safe fresh-directory setup
code.code:
set -eu
DIR="devin-operating-card-exercise"
if [ -e "$DIR" ]; then
  printf '%s\n' "Refusing to continue: directory already exists: $DIR" >&2
  exit 1
fi
mkdir "$DIR"
printf '%s\n' '{"type":"commonjs"}' > "$DIR/package.json"
printf '%s\n' "Created $DIR with local CommonJS mode. Save shipping.js, shipping.test.js, and shipping.answer.js there, then run: cd $DIR && node shipping.test.js"

sections.title: Local module-mode declaration
paragraphs: The setup creates this file automatically. It is shown separately so the learner can inspect the setting that makes the exercise files CommonJS regardless of a type:module parent repository.

sections.title: Starter file with deliberate failure
paragraphs: Save the following complete file as shipping.js. The OR operator is the intentional defect. It allows an order with hold equal to false even when its status is not ready, and it allows a ready order whose hold is true.

code.label: shipping.js

sections.title: Immutable positive, negative, and changed-input tests
paragraphs: Save this complete file as shipping.test.js and do not modify it. It uses Node's built-in assert/strict module and strictEqual for exact actual-versus-expected comparison. Each case is attempted even when an earlier case fails. The broken baseline therefore reports one passing case and two failures. A successful repaired run prints one exact success line.

code.label: shipping.test.js

sections.title: Repair step and exact outcomes
paragraphs:
From the exercise directory, run node shipping.test.js with the starter file. The deterministic broken-baseline output is exactly:
PASS: positive: ready and not held
FAIL: negative: ready but held: expected false, got true
FAIL: changed input: packed instead of ready: expected false, got true
FAILURES: 2
The process exits with status 1. The first failure shows that the OR predicate accepts a held ready order. The second shows that it accepts a packed order when hold is false. The causal feedback is that the implementation accepts either condition while the requirement needs both conditions.

Repair only the predicate in shipping.js by changing the OR operator to an AND operator. Do not change the function name, module export, test file, or expected values. Then run node shipping.test.js again.

Exact repaired outcome is a successful process exit with status 0 and this final line after the three per-case lines:
PASS: 3 immutable shipping eligibility cases
The logical results are true for {status: "ready", hold: false}, false for {status: "ready", hold: true}, and false for {status: "packed", hold: false}. These outcomes follow from inspection of the supplied files. They are not a claim that commands were executed by the author.

code.label: Expected broken-baseline output
code.code:
PASS: positive: ready and not held
FAIL: negative: ready but held: expected false, got true
FAIL: changed input: packed instead of ready: expected false, got true
FAILURES: 2

sections.title: Separate answer file
paragraphs: Keep the answer separate from the learner workflow. Save this complete file as shipping.answer.js only after attempting the repair, or compare its predicate with shipping.js during review. The answer is not required by the test runner.

code.label: shipping.answer.js

sections.title: What this exercise does and does not prove
paragraphs: Local evidence consists of the copied source files, the immutable test file, the local package.json, the command used, and the resulting exit status and output. A learner can inspect the diff between the starter and repaired shipping.js and explain why each case changes or remains correct.

This simulation does not prove that Devin can access a particular repository, attach a particular Knowledge or Playbook, create or protect a branch, open or review a pull request, enforce permissions, monitor a session, or reverse external side effects. Those claims require a dated authoritative product source or an actual authorized session record.

For a real delegation, record the task prompt, approved repository and revision, applicable Knowledge and Playbook identifiers, authorized scope, session activity, branch diff, test output, reviewer decision, and external postcondition checks. Do not fabricate any missing record. Label an absent item UNKNOWN and identify the verification needed.

sections.title: Primary sources and verification
paragraphs: Cognition, Your first Devin session: https://docs.devin.ai/get-started/first-run. This source supports Devin's repository-based software engineering work, asking for scopes, repository inquiry and planning, choosing a repository and agent, modifying code, running commands, and creating pull requests. It was checked on 2026-09-20 according to the supplied research findings.

Cognition, Creating Devin Playbooks: https://docs.devin.ai/product-guides/creating-playbooks. This source supports Playbooks as reusable guides containing an outcome, procedure, specifications, advice, forbidden actions, and required user input, and supports attaching and inspecting them before starting. It was checked on 2026-09-20 according to the supplied research findings.
Node.js assert documentation: https://nodejs.org/api/assert.html#assertstrictequalactual-expected-message. The exercise uses assert/strict and strictEqual for exact comparisons.

Node.js modules documentation: https://nodejs.org/api/modules.html. The exercise uses CommonJS require and module.exports. The local package.json explicitly selects commonjs for the exercise directory.
Node.js process documentation: https://nodejs.org/api/process.html#process_exit_code. The test uses process.exitCode to report a failing run without stopping before all cases are reported.
